title: markdownpoint/agent/1
description: MarkdownPoint’s agent contract: each method with the scope it is served in, the params it takes and the result it answers, the envelope a request and its response travel in, and the error a failure gives.

schema.description: The answer is a JSON Schema, the contract describing itself.

ids.description: The sections, comments, slides, objects and steps the change created or deleted.

locked.description: The objects the change left as they were because they are locked.

revision.description: The presentation's revision with the change in it.

value.description: Effective value in authored parameter space before its groups' transforms; omitted when no value or default exists.

valueType.description: What kind of value the parameter holds, which says how its keyframes blend: a discrete value holds until the next keyframe.

app.description: The app that answers: its version, as `mdpoint --version` and MCP's server info give it.

interpolations.description: The named interpolations; a keyframe may instead carry four cubic-bezier numbers [x1, y1, x2, y2] with x within 0–1.

methods.description: What the app serves itself, with no presentation, and what it serves for one.

operations.description: Operation types `proposals.create` takes; `schema` serves each one's exact request contract.

AgentCapabilities.description: The app's contract, the same whichever presentation is open, or none.

id.description: The id of the movie export to cancel, as its exports.run request gave it.

canceled.description: True means cancellation was requested for the matching active movie; its original awaited response reports the outcome.

duration.description: How long the movie plays, in seconds.

hiddenTextSlides.description: The slides, by number, whose words a slide's edge, the end of a path or a table cell hides (`text-hidden`).

fonts.description: The fonts the file carries, which PowerPoint shows wherever it opens.

missingFonts.description: The families the theme names that the file does not carry; their words are set in the fonts MarkdownPoint includes.

hiddenTextSlides.description: The slides, by number, whose words a slide's edge, the end of a path or a table cell hides (`text-hidden`).
The slides, by number, whose words a slide's edge, the end of a path or a table cell hides (`text-hidden`).

AgentFootSlip.description: How fast a walking model's planted foot slides across the floor against how fast its body travels, canvas units a second. The foot is a joint of the model's file, `node` its glTF node index, which tells two feet named alike apart, and `foot` its name as the file spells it, or "(node N)" for an unnamed one.

AgentFrame.description: A box on the slide in canvas units, as MarkdownPoint measures it: an object's, its words' or a model's bounds.

dropped.description: The display frames the playback missed, at the refresh rate of the display the show is on: each interval's refresh periods, rounded to whole ones, past the first. Null when that display gives no refresh rate.

interval.description: The time from one frame to the next, in milliseconds.

paint.description: How long each frame took to paint, in milliseconds.

AgentFrameProbe.description: How the audience window painted its last continuous playback, from each frame's own timestamp.

themeRevision.description: Needed when the step is a theme edit: `themeRevision` from `themes.get` or `themes.edit`.

AgentHistoryRequest.description: Edit > Undo or Redo: the presentation's one history, slide and theme steps alike. It moves only while nothing changed since the revisions given, so an agent undoing its own change never undoes someone else's later edit.

status.description: noChange when there was no step to take. discarded when another window, a collaborator or an outside edit has since deleted everything the step on top changed. The call drops that step from the history without taking it, and the next call takes the step beneath.

AgentImageEditor.description: The external image editor, which only the app's own chooser sets.

objectId.description: An image object on that slide.

token.description: The token images.prepare returned; it is spent once and expires.

status.description: applied when the image is in place, one reused for the same settings among them; noChange when it is kept among the variants, unused, as when the target changed while it was made, and images.select puts it in place by its generationId.

AgentImagePrepareResult.description: What generating would do, as the app's confirmation shows it: the provider and model it would use, whether it pays a provider (`requiresProvider`) or reuses an image already made for the same settings, and a `token` that `images.generate` spends. The prompt, transparency and style are the target's own properties, set as edits.

objectId.description: An image object on that slide; omit for the slide's background.

restyled.description: true for the restyle of the image or the slide's background, made from its image as first made, rather than its prompt.

slideId.description: The slide the image or background is on.

status.description: noChange when the image already shows the variant.

output.description: Absolute path of a new .json file outside any presentation folder.

path.description: Absolute path of a styles file.

definition.description: A style definition as images.styles.list lists them.

id.description: A style id from images.styles.list: the style to duplicate, delete or preview, the one save writes over, or the one export writes alone.

AgentImageStylesEditRequest.description: The Choose style… dialog's commands on the saved styles, which belong to this machine as its themes do: save a definition (as a new style, or over `id`), duplicate, delete, generate a style's preview pair (spending on OpenAI, as the dialog's Generate preview does), import a styles file and export one style or all to a file.

AgentImageStylesEditResult.description: The styles after the change; `selectedId` is the one saved, duplicated, imported or previewed, and `files` the export's file.

AgentImageStylesResult.description: The style library, as the Restyle popup lists it; set one's `definition` as an image's `restyle`.

slideId.description: The slide whose words the prompt is drawn from.

objectId.description: An image object on that slide; omit for the slide's background.

restyled.description: true for the restyle of the image or the slide's background, made from its image as first made, rather than its prompt.

slideId.description: The slide the image or background is on.

AgentImageTarget.description: The image a generation is for, as the inspector's image sections name it: an image object by `objectId` on `slideId`, or the slide's background by `slideId` alone. `restyled` is its restyle, generated from its current image as its Restyle section does, rather than from its prompt.

AgentImageVariant.description: A generated image kept for the target, as the variant strip shows them; `current` is the one in use. `created` is when it was made, left out where its record doesn't say.

fileScope.description: A file's issue: whose folder the file it is about is in, since each may hold a file of that path.

location.description: Where the problem stands, when its line is known.

AgentIssue.description: A problem with the presentation as the contract gives it: its English, where it stands and what the app does about it.

ink.description: The box of its ink, the font's own outline, upright on the slide; absent for a letter that draws nothing.

pen.description: Its pen, on the baseline it stands on.

text.description: The graphemes it draws: one, or several for a ligature.

AgentLetter.description: A letter of a text where its slide draws it at rest, in canvas units: what a model sits on, lands on or points at.

bevel.description: How far their edges bevel, 0.02 when left out.

depth.description: How deep the letters extrude, 0.2 when left out.

data.description: With for and no source, the letters' depth and bevel, in ems of the text's size.

for.description: A text object whose words a build makes 3D: data.words holds its letters, as its page lays them out at rest.

models.description: The presentation's models the build loads with kit.model, by file path, such as a model models_animate gave actions.

name.description: The model's file name without extension, such as bird.

AgentLetterBuildRequest.description: A text's words the app's letter builder makes 3D: kit.text(data.words, { depth, bevel }).

envelopeBytes.description: An envelope travels as one line, one string, so it is at most the longest string, counted in bytes: an ASCII envelope's characters.

heldProposals.description: Proposals waiting at once: each stays in memory until it is accepted or rejected.

longestEdge.description: The longest edge a rendered slide or frame can have: the longest side any export writes.

proposalOperations.description: Operations one proposal carries: it is applied as one batch.

rangeSamples.description: Samples one `slides.frames` or `slides.measure` request takes: each renders the slide, and a frame's PNG is held until the answer is sent.

traceSamples.description: Samples one `slides.trace` request reads: each samples the whole animation once, and a frame rate times a range could reach billions.

AgentLongestEdge.description: The longest edge of a rendered picture in pixels, the slide's aspect ratio kept, up to capabilities' limits.longestEdge.

data.description: The file's bytes in base64, with name.

name.description: File name with the media's extension, such as photo.png, with data in place of path.

path.description: Absolute path of the media file on this machine; or name and data in its place.

AgentMediaImportRequest.description: An image, video or audio file copied into the presentation's folder, as the media picker or a drop copies one: from a file on this machine by its absolute path, or from its bytes (base64) under a file name whose extension names its kind.

AgentMediaImportResult.description: The file's path in the presentation, as an object names it, and the object type it makes; `warnings` says what the import kept without, such as a movie's poster.

AgentMeshyActionId.description: An action of Meshy's library, by the whole-number id models_actions lists it by.

AgentMeshyActions.description: Actions of Meshy's library for one task, each once.

AgentMintedId.description: A lowercase UUID the app minted.

filter.description: Words the action's name or category must hold, such as walk inplace.

AgentModelActionsRequest.description: Meshy's actions whose name or category holds every word of `filter`.

actions.description: Action ids from models_actions, in the order the Actions should come.

file.description: A model models_rig made, or one models_animate made from it.

looping.description: Names of the Actions that loop, closed on their cycle, as models_actions names them.

name.description: The animated model's file name; the model's when left out.

AgentModelAnimateRequest.description: Actions of Meshy's library, by id, on a model Meshy rigged; `looping` names the Actions to close on their cycle.

AgentModelBuildRequest.description: A model to build in the build window, saved as media/<name>-<hash>.glb: from source, or a text's words, from source or by the app's letter builder, saved as generated/<name>-<hash>.glb.

builtFrom.description: With for: the value the text's model carries as its `built-from`, in `model: { file, "built-from" }`, to show while its words are these.

violations.description: What the window's policy refused while the build ran.

AgentModelBuildResult.description: The saved model, what import changed in the build's GLB, what the model does, and its sheet.

character.description: A figure to rig, in a T-pose.

file.description: A picture of the presentation in place of picture, such as media/rocket-1a2b3c4d.png.

name.description: The model's file name without extension, such as rocket.

AgentModelFromFileRequest.description: A model from a picture of the presentation.

character.description: A figure to rig, in a T-pose.

name.description: The model's file name without extension, such as rocket.

AgentModelFromPictureRequest.description: A model from the picture models_picture returned.

AgentModelGenerateRequest.description: A model Meshy makes from a picture, saved as media/<name>-<hash>.glb: `pictureId` from models_picture, or `file`, an image of the presentation. A character's comes in a T-pose, ready for models_rig.

file.description: The model's path, such as media/bird-1a2b3c4d.glb.

AgentModelInspectRequest.description: A model of the presentation, by its file's path.

bounds.description: The exact box around every vertex at rest.

castShadowOff.description: The nodes whose extras.markdownpoint set `"cast-shadow": false`: they cast no shadow.

colorRoles.description: The color roles its materials name.

bevel.description: How far their edges bevel, 0.02 when left out.

depth.description: How deep the letters extrude, 0.2 when left out.

hiddenAtRest.description: Parts at rest scaled to nothing, as glTF has no visibility of its own: only the topmost of them.

AgentModelInspectResult.description: What a model does. For letters the app built: the text they came from, and their depth and bevel.

floorGap.description: How far its lowest point stands above the slide's floor, its highest floor object, in canvas units.

file.description: The model to rig, such as media/figure-1a2b3c4d.glb.

name.description: The rigged model's file name; the model's with -rigged when left out.

AgentModelRigRequest.description: A model of the presentation for Meshy to rig, a humanoid facing +Z, `height` meters tall.

transition.description: A slide transition. A scroll moves both slides along one strip. Each slide's 3D objects keep their index in its stacking order and are clipped at its edge. A model or 3D text with the same id on both slides crosses between them whole. Neither slide's camera drifts during a scroll. During any other transition, both cameras drift. Keys left out default to interpolation ease-in-out, match object, direction left, color black, and delay 0.

delay.description: For a transition that starts by itself, how long it waits after the slide's last step ends.

AgentSlideObject.description: An object as the .mdpoint file spells it, with its words when it holds text (a text box, a shape, a table, a chart): exactly the Markdown setText takes, so writing it back unchanged changes nothing; "" for empty words. A paragraph's `<!-- id: … -->` at the end of its last line is the id a step's text cue names it by, and it travels with its paragraph. In words written without ids, an unchanged paragraph keeps its id wherever it moves. Every other paragraph keeps its id where its words start: a split's first part keeps it, and a join keeps the first paragraph's. Give a new paragraph none, so the app gives it one and its own step. Words that leave out a paragraph a step's cue names are refused, naming the step: keep the paragraph's id, or remove the cue first.

longestEdge.description: Maximum PNG edge in pixels, preserving the slide's aspect ratio. Defaults to 1024.

output.description: Absolute path of a new .png file outside any presentation folder, which the app writes instead of returning the image inline; the result then names it in files and carries no image.

fittedFrames.description: The frame each text object takes when fitted to its text at this position, in its own parameters there, to write as transformObjects' `drawnFrame` at the same position: `height` as Fit box to text and the bottom handle fit it, the top kept; `width` as a side handle fits it, every paragraph on one line, the point its alignment holds kept. Its letters stay where they stand whatever its turn, scale and anchor. A box that grows to its words already stands at its `height`, the height its words take, which no file holds. Text in columns has no `width`; objects with no text are left out.

overflowing.description: Objects whose text does not fit their frames at this position, taller or wider than the box, as the canvas marks them.

textBounds.description: Where each object's words stand on the slide at this position, in canvas units: the axis-aligned box around its lines' boxes as the slide draws them, after every turn, scale and move of the object and its groups. Objects with no words are left out.

fittedFrames.description: The frame each text object takes when fitted to its text at this position, in its own parameters there, to write as transformObjects' `drawnFrame` at the same position: `height` as Fit box to text and the bottom handle fit it, the top kept; `width` as a side handle fits it, every paragraph on one line, the point its alignment holds kept. Its letters stay where they stand whatever its turn, scale and anchor. A box that grows to its words already stands at its `height`, the height its words take, which no file holds. Text in columns has no `width`; objects with no text are left out.

overflowing.description: Objects whose text does not fit their frames at this position, taller or wider than the box, as the canvas marks them.

textBounds.description: Where each object's words stand on the slide at this position, in canvas units: the axis-aligned box around its lines' boxes as the slide draws them, after every turn, scale and move of the object and its groups. Objects with no words are left out.

AgentSlideRenderResult.description: The PNG in the answer, or with an output the one file written, in `files`.

animationValueSchemas.description: Each parameter's value domain by object type, then by parameter, once for each type on the slide that has it: a type holds its own range where it differs, as a text's scale and a model's do. A dry run still checks each value against its own object.

drawnEnds.description: Where each line's ends are drawn as authored, whatever `moment` names, by id: a free end where auto layout places it, an end on an object where it meets that object.

drawnFrames.description: Where each object a transform moves by a frame is drawn as authored, whatever `moment` names, by id: the frame transformObjects' `drawnFrame` takes and gives back, in the same space, its turn and scale apart. A growing text box stands at the size its words take, a table at its rows' height, a group at the box its members give it, an object auto layout places where it places it. A travel's `drawnPoints` are where this frame's corner goes.

moment.description: Null is Base. A sampled moment reports the actual clamped time; Start has null stepId and time zero.

objects.description: The slide's objects as authored, before any animation, whatever `moment` names: groups and each object's parent included, with the ids an edit names, each as the .mdpoint file spells it, a growing text's `frame` the point its growth holds, and an object auto layout places where its file stores it; the values at the `moment` are each target's `animationParameters` value.

playbackStepIds.description: Ordered steps that consume presenter advances. Dormant authored steps remain in steps for editing.

fileScopes.description: Whose folder each file an object names is in, by the key that names it; a key the object doesn't hold is absent.

provenance.description: Which theme level owns each object. Master and layout objects are the theme's; only a placeholder takes setText. `fileScopes` says whose folder each file the object names is in, by the key that names it: a path is the theme's (in the theme's folder, as its `theme` key names it) or the presentation's. Each level's own file stays in its own folder, so a slide's poster over a layout's video is the presentation's while the video is the theme's.

step-duration.description: How long a step's fade or move takes, in seconds: the master's step-duration, or the format's default.

steps.description: Ordered authored animation data from the same document and revision as the scene, in the file's words.

trimStops.description: For each drawing, where its points fall along each contour as fractions of the contour's length: the values a trim keyframe takes to stop at a point.

parameters.description: Each parameter with keyframes in the step, sampled at every time in authored parameter space, before its groups' transforms.

AgentSlideView.description: slide (the default) as the audience sees it; top or left for the slide's 3D content from above, the audience at the bottom, or from the slide's left, the audience on the right, with the slide's plane and its shadow catchers' planes drawn in and lines from the slide's corners toward its camera, to judge depth a front view hides. A slide with no 3D content has no top or side view.

after.description: The step that leads the click it follows; null for the wait as the slide has appeared.

before.description: The step that leads the click that ends it; null after the last.

hold.description: Why the slide's 3D holds still at the wait while something in it would move on, as the slide's warning says, whatever its 2D does.

samples.description: Each moment measured, `time` seconds into the wait: how much of each object draws, 0 to 1, its opacity and its groups', 0 while hidden; and each model and 3D text's measures, as `slides_measure` gives them for a step.

slideAge.description: Seconds since the slide began to appear, as it settles.

AgentSlideWait.description: Where a show holds the slide until the next click, or after its last: once the click's steps, their "with" and "after" members, its Actions and the camera's drift have all ended. Measured as it settles, and over one period while it loops: the period of the 3D's loop, or of the 2D's while the 3D stands still, held or at rest. Where both loop at lengths of their own, the period is the 3D's, the 2D measured on its own clock.

fps.description: Frames a second it samples over a wait that loops, 30 when omitted.

waits.description: Measure the slide at every wait for a click its show makes instead of a step; omit stepId, from and to.

AgentSlideWaitsRequest.description: A slide measured at each wait for a click its show makes, in place of a step's range: over a wait that loops, `fps` frames a second, 30 when omitted.

AgentSlidesResizeRequest.description: Slide size, as the Presentation panel changes it: the theme and the slides scale together. A change of aspect needs rescale: fit keeps everything on the slide, fill covers it.

rescaled.description: The policy the slides were rescaled by; null when nothing changed.

status.description: noChange when the slides already have the size.

fps.description: Frames a second it samples, 30 when omitted.

from.description: Seconds within the step where the range starts. Defaults to 0.

longestEdge.description: Maximum frame edge in pixels, preserving the slide's aspect ratio. Defaults to 512.

output.description: A new or empty folder outside any presentation folder, which the frames are written into as frame-0001.png onward beside sheet.png; the result names them in files. Omitted, only the sheet returns.

stepId.description: The step whose time is sampled, from slides.get.

to.description: Seconds within the step where the range ends, inclusive. Defaults to the end of the step's last pass.

AgentStepId.description: A step's stable id, as `slides.get` lists it.

fps.description: Frames a second it samples over a step, 10 when omitted.

from.description: Seconds within the step where the range starts. Defaults to 0.

stepId.description: The step whose time is sampled, from slides.get.

to.description: Seconds within the step where the range ends, inclusive. Defaults to the end of the step's last pass.

AgentStepMeasureRequest.description: A step's range as `slides.measure` samples it, 10 times a second by default.

fps.description: Frames a second it samples, 30 when omitted.

from.description: Seconds within the step where the range starts. Defaults to 0.

stepId.description: The step whose time is sampled, from slides.get.

to.description: Seconds within the step where the range ends, inclusive. Defaults to the end of the step's last pass.

AgentStepRange.description: A span of one step's time, sampled at a rate: `from` 0 and `to` the end of its last pass when omitted, 30 per second.

AgentStepSeconds.description: Seconds within a step, as the step's own times read them.

AgentTextCover.description: How much of a text's box a model's bounds overlap, how much of the text the model covers, and how much of its box the model's shadow does, 0 to 1. A model covers flat words where its silhouette lies over their box, in front or behind, and 3D words, which their own model draws, where it draws in front of their letters.

AgentTextOverflowIssue.description: A presentations.get warning about words that run past their frame, where they still show; about words something hides, the slide's edge, the end of their path or their table cell, which an export asks about; or that this could not be measured.

data.description: With for, a record, to which data.words adds the text's letters.

for.description: A text object whose words a build makes 3D: data.words holds its letters, as its page lays them out at rest.

models.description: The presentation's models the build loads with kit.model, by file path, such as a model models_animate gave actions.

name.description: The model's file name without extension, such as bird.

source.description: The build: an ES module with a default export build(kit, data). No file keeps it.

AgentTextSourceBuildRequest.description: A text's words its source makes 3D.

AgentTextSummary.description: The most any model covers a text, when and which, and the spans of time one is `over` it; and the same of their shadows, in `shadow`.

master.description: The master's settings as the file names them.

themeRevision.description: Guards `themes.edit`, and the theme step of `history.undo`/`history.redo`.

AgentThemeGetResult.description: The presentation's theme as Edit theme edits it: the master and each layout, authored values only.

current.description: The key of the theme the presentation uses; null when its master is in no listed theme.

name.description: The theme's name for create and rename; the layout's name for saveSlide.

output.description: Absolute path of a new .mdptheme file outside any presentation folder; the result names it in files.

theme.description: A theme's key or name from themes.list.

from.description: The theme key or name the layout is in.

layout.description: The layout's key in from, as themes.list gives it.

to.description: The theme key or name it goes to.

AgentThemeManageRequest.description: The theme chooser's own commands, and Save slide as layout. A new theme starts as a copy of the one in use; a layout is copied or moved into another theme by its key from `themes.list`; export writes a .mdptheme file and install adds one, from paths where the app would ask with a dialog.

layout.description: The layout's key in the theme it was copied, moved or saved to, which setSlideLayout and insertSlide take.

theme.description: The theme created, renamed, installed or given the layout; the one exported. By its key and name.

id.description: Its master's id, a lowercase UUID, as `presentations.get` gives the master in use; null while its master cannot be read.

key.description: The theme's key, its folder's name; `themes.use` and `themes.manage` take it or the name.

layouts.description: Its layouts, by the key the slides, `themes.manage` and `themes.edit` name them by.

size.description: The theme's slide size; null while its master cannot be read.

AgentThemeSummary.description: One theme the presentation can change to: the themes its chooser lists.

rescale.description: Required when the theme's slide size differs: fit keeps everything on the slide, fill covers it.

theme.description: A theme's key or name from `themes.list`.

AgentThemeUseRequest.description: Change the presentation's theme, as the app's theme chooser does; slides keep their layouts by key.

rescaled.description: The policy the slides were rescaled by; null when the sizes matched.

status.description: noChange when the presentation already uses the theme.

theme.description: The theme the presentation uses now, by its key and name.

fps.description: Frames a second it samples, 30 when omitted.

from.description: Seconds within the step where the range starts. Defaults to 0.

longestEdge.description: Maximum frame edge in pixels, preserving the slide's aspect ratio. Defaults to 512.

output.description: A new or empty folder outside any presentation folder, which the frames are written into as frame-0001.png onward beside sheet.png; the result names them in files. Omitted, only the sheet returns.

to.description: Seconds within the step where the range ends, inclusive. Defaults to the end of the step's last pass.

transition.description: Render the slide's transition into the next shown slide instead of a step, from 0 to its duration in seconds; omit stepId and view.

AgentTransitionFramesRequest.description: Frames of the slide's transition into the next shown slide, in place of a step's.

AgentWaitHold.description: What moves on at a wait in a way no video of a show repeats, so its 3D holds still until the next click: the objects a step's wait loop moves (`looped`) and Actions a camera follows on a spring (`followed`), which keep their timing, that line up within no loop a show renders; a walk whose travel its step's loop moves on and on; the camera, whose spring doesn't settle; or an Action whose length isn't known, as its model's file lacks it or isn't read. Each names the objects to change.

AgentWaitTextSummary.description: The most any model covers a text at the slide's waits, as a sample's `covered` says, and its shadow does, and where: `waitIndex` is the wait's place in `waits`. Counted only while both draw.

AgentWalkSpeed.description: The speed an in-place walk travels at this model's size, at which its planted feet hold.

AgentWindow.description: A document window, as `windows.list` gives it: the presentation it shows, or null, and whether it is focused.

ColorSource.description: A color as the file spells it: a theme color by name, as `accent`, or a hex color, as `"#2F7D4F"`.

ConstraintStrengthParameter.description: A model's constraint's strength, by the constraint's id, as `constraints.<id>.strength`.

files.description: Its own pictures by object id: one file, or one per scheme.

name.description: The name the chooser shows: the file's, or one spelled from the key.

objects.description: Its own objects, back to front.

EditableLayout.description: A layout as its pane and inspector show it.

id.description: The placeholder object's id, which a slide fills it by.

type.description: The placeholder object's type, as the layout file spells it: words or a picture.

EditableLayoutPlaceholder.description: One placeholder of a layout, which a slide fills by its id.

files.description: The master's own pictures by object id: one file, or one per scheme.

key.description: The theme's key, its folder's name.

objects.description: Its own objects, back to front, whose names a layout's placeholder can't take.

schemes.description: `light`, `dark`, then every named scheme in file order.

size.description: The slide size in canvas units, as the file's `size`.

step-duration.description: How long a slide step's fade or move takes; null takes the format's default.

EditableMasterSource.description: The master as the file names its settings, for the Agent: its `layout-order` and `text-styles`, its guides and grid as the file writes them, and its `step-duration`.

FillSource.description: A fill as the file spells it: `none`, one color, or a gradient whose stops name their colors.

bounds.description: The box around every vertex over the whole Action; left out for a model with no vertices, as the report's own is.

duration.description: Its last keyframe: how long it plays from the file's 0.

loop.description: The Action's own `loop` in its extras.markdownpoint, or null when it says neither.

lowest.description: Its lowest point and when, against a floor at y = 0; left out for a model with no vertices.

name.description: The Action's name, unique among the model's, which a clip plays it by: a name the file gives is kept, and every such name is reserved first; an unnamed Action is "Animation" and its number in the file, from 1, as "Animation 1"; a name an earlier Action has, or a generated name already reserved or given, takes the first of " 2", " 3" and on not yet taken.

seam.description: How far any vertex is between the Action's first frame and its last: what a loop jumps by.

start.description: Its first keyframe, in seconds on the file's clock. An Action's time 0 is the file's 0, so it may start late.

stride.description: For a model with feet, what its Action does with them.

weights.description: The range of the morph weights it plays, or null when it has none.

GlbFoot.description: A foot of a walk: the joint by its node index and name, as every node of the report is named; how much of the Action it stands planted, and how fast it slides then.

GlbNodeName.description: A node of the model's file: its glTF node index, which names it exactly, two parts named alike or unnamed among them, and its name as the file spells it, or "(node N)" for an unnamed one, for a reader.

bounds.description: The exact box around every vertex at rest.

castShadowOff.description: The nodes whose extras.markdownpoint set `"cast-shadow": false`: they cast no shadow.

colorRoles.description: The color roles its materials name.

height.description: The rest height, and whether the model stands on y = 0 within a hundredth of it.

hiddenAtRest.description: Parts at rest scaled to nothing, as glTF has no visibility of its own: only the topmost of them.

GlbStride.description: How far a walk or run played in place carries the character per loop, in the model's units: `inPlace` when its planted feet slide back at one speed, `rootMotion` when the Action moves the character itself, `none` otherwise.

GradientCenter.description: Where a radial gradient centers: a point in the box it paints, in fractions of it across and down, 0 at its top left.

position.description: Where the stop stands along the gradient, 0–1.
Where the stop stands along the gradient, 0–1.

GradientFillSource.description: A gradient as the file spells it: its type, and stops that name their colors.

GradientLine.description: A linear gradient's own line: centered at (`x`, `y`) in frame fractions, `length` frame diagonals long. It may reach past the frame, holds while an outline morphs, and turns about its center with the angle.

IssueLocation.description: Where in a presentation's files an issue stands: the file's name, and its line, counted from 1, and column when known.

IssueSource.description: What raised an issue, which says how the issue names where it stands.

MasterAuthoredFont.description: The settings of a theme's master and layouts as their editors change them: the master's fonts, colors, text styles, guides, grid, step duration and layout order, a layout's name and scheme, which of its words and pictures are placeholders, and a theme picture's file per scheme. Each edit changes the file's authored values and is accepted only when the file it leaves reads back, so no edit writes a file the next read would refuse.

colors.description: Its colors by role, as authored: a CSS hex or `{brand.<name>}`.

marks.description: Each mark's values, as the master file holds them.

properties.description: Its own properties' values, as the master file holds them.

MasterGridSource.description: A grid as the file writes it: its columns, with a gutter and margin of 0 when left out, and its baseline from its start at its increment.

MasterGuideSource.description: A guide as the file writes it: at `x` an upright line, at `y` a level one.

MasterTextStyleValue.description: A text style's value as the master file holds it: a size, weight, measure or spacing as a number (`44`, `1.05`), a font role, case or bullet as its word, and a color as a role or a hex color.

ObjectAnimationValueType.description: What kind of value a parameter holds, which says how it passes between keyframes, as three.js's ValueTypeName does: a `discrete` value, a flag, a word or a record, holds until the next keyframe, as a discrete curve does in Unity; a `paint` passes as a color between two colors and as a fill between two gradients.

PresentationAnimationBackInterpolation.description: Blender's Back with its Back setting: how far anticipate winds up, overshoot swings past its keyframe, or both.

PresentationAnimationBezier.description: A cubic Bézier interpolation as CSS spells it: two control points with time on x within 0–1 and value on y, which may overshoot.

PresentationAnimationBounceInterpolation.description: A bounce at a bounciness, Blender's Rigid Body word for a rebound's share of the speed it lands with; Blender's Bounce at 0.5.

id.description: Caller-minted stable ID, unique together with keyframes in this step.

time.description: Nonnegative seconds, kept to the microsecond.

PresentationAnimationCurveInterpolation.description: A named curve with its settings, the keyframe-interpolation record: Blender's Back with its back, its Elastic with an amplitude and a period, a bounce with a bounciness, or a spring.

PresentationAnimationCurveSource.description: A curve as the file spells it: its keyframes, its loop's word and the keyframe that loop starts from, the first when it names none.

PresentationAnimationElasticInterpolatio.description: Blender's Elastic ringing into its keyframe: its ring as a multiple of the move, and its length in seconds, or 0.3 of the move.

exponential-scale.description: Whether the move to this keyframe scales at an even rate, as After Effects' Exponential Scale does.

id.description: Caller-minted stable ID; new keyframes/cues share one unique namespace within the step. Reusing an ID replaces the whole event.

interpolation.description: Interpolation into this keyframe, from the preceding keyframe or the step's start.

end.description: When it would have ended, in step seconds, at or after the keyframe's time; it does not extend the step.

interrupted.description: The longer move this keyframe interrupts: up to this keyframe, the motion follows that move's curve.

oscillate.description: An oscillation added from this keyframe on, its wave named as the file names it.

path.description: On a point keyframe, `frame.xy`, `translation.xy` or `position.xyz`: the move into it bends along this path.

start.description: When the move into this keyframe begins, in step seconds; until then the value before it holds. Absent, at the keyframe before.

time.description: Nonnegative seconds, kept to the microsecond.

value.description: Null clears an optional property; its current text-style/default then applies.

PresentationAnimationKeyframeSource.description: A keyframe as the file spells it: a move's `end` and `exponential-scale`, and a fill as the object spells its fill.

frequency.description: Cycles a second, as After Effects' wiggle() frequency sets it; a noise wanders at that rate.

phase.description: Degrees into the cycle at the keyframe.

seed.description: Which noise a noise wave draws, as Motion's Random Seed picks one; the same seed always draws the same.

PresentationAnimationOscillationSource.description: An oscillation as the file spells it: its wave is `wave-shape`.

anyOf.description: A geometry parameter as the file names it: a line's ends are its start and end.

PresentationAnimationParameterSource.description: A parameter as the file names it: `stroke-weight`, `crop.focal-point.x`, `frame.x`.

orient.description: Turn the object to face along the path as it moves.

PresentationAnimationPath.description: A path in chord space: the start is (0, 0), the end (1, 0), and one unit across is a chord length right of travel.

PresentationAnimationPoint.description: A point keyframe's value: a frame's or a translation's x and y, or a 3D position's x, y and z.

PresentationAnimationSpring.description: A spring landing on its keyframe: `amount` sets how far it swings past, from 0, which settles with no overshoot, to 1, and `response` its period in seconds as SwiftUI's does, or it fits the keyframe.

PresentationAnimationTargetSource.description: A curve's target as the file names it: its object's id is `object`.

anyOf.description: What a keyframe holds: a number, a flag, a color or a role, a fill, lengths, a shadow, a 3D object's whole orientation, or a point.

PresentationAnimationValueSource.description: A value as the file spells it: a fill as `accent` or a gradient whose stops name their colors.

PresentationCommentAddress.description: A thread, or one of its replies, by the thread's id, unique among the presentation's threads.

id.description: Who they are: `local:` and a lowercase UUID for a computer's user, `shared:` and 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits for a collaboration service member, or `dropbox:` and a Dropbox account id; absent when the writer knows none.

name.description: The name they wrote it under.

PresentationCommentPosition.description: Fractions of the slide's width and height, independent of its current size.

color.description: A color role or an opaque CSS hex: a role's own opacity doesn't reach the shadow, whose opacity is its only one.

offset.description: Across and down from the object, in the object's own turn.

size.description: How far past what casts it the shadow reaches, as Photoshop's Size.

spread.description: The share of the size, 0–1, by which what casts the shadow grows solid before the rest of the size blurs, as Photoshop's Spread: at 1 the shadow stands solid all the way out. None where left out.

PresentationDropShadow.description: A drop shadow, as Photoshop's Layer Style › Drop Shadow sets one: how far it reaches, how much of that reach stands solid, how far each way it falls and in what color. Its lengths are canvas units, and a text's are ems of its size.

PresentationNavigationSlide.description: A slide's entry; a composition stands in no section and follows the slides.

PresentationObjectLevel.description: Where an object the slide shows, its own or inherited, came from, and which of its properties the slide overrides.

PresentationOrientation.description: A 3D object's orientation in quaternion mode, whole, its w with x, y and z: a quaternion of length 1.

PresentationSection.description: A section of the presentation: the .md file's header, its id and the name its heading line gives it.

PresentationStepCueSource.description: What a cue starts, as the file spells it: its `type`, and a clip's `clip-trim`, `blend-in` and `clip-scale`.

min-duration.description: The least seconds the step lasts; left out or 0, it lasts as long as what it holds.

repeat.description: Play the step this many times before it completes; omitted plays once.

start.description: Plays without a click of its own: with the step before it, or after that step ends, as PowerPoint's With Previous and After Previous do. Its times then count from that start. On the first step it plays after the transition. Omitted, the step waits for a click.

PresentationStepSource.description: A step as its file writes it.

PresentationWaitHold.description: What moves on at a wait in a way no video repeats, so the 3D layer holds still until the next click: wait loops and repeats a camera follows on a spring, which keep their timing, that come round together within no loop the video may render, by the objects they move; a walk paced by a travel that loops; a camera whose spring doesn't settle; or an Action whose length isn't known, as its model's file lacks it or isn't read.

RenderFileScope.description: Whose folder a file is in: the presentation's, its theme's, or the cache where MarkdownPoint keeps the models it builds from a text's letters on this computer.

SlideSize.description: A slide's size in canvas units.

ThemeFile.description: A theme's own picture: one theme-relative file, or one per scheme, `light` and `dark` among them.

end.description: The file's or the Action's end when absent.

TimeTrim.description: The span of a movie's or an audio object's file, or of a model's Action, that plays, in seconds. Its end, when given, is after its start. A loop repeats it.

color.description: a color role or a hex color

additionalProperties.description: one line with one space between words, none at the start or end, and no "-->"

model-node-name.description: the name of one of the model’s nodes

opaque-color.description: a color role or a hex color without opacity, such as "#000000"

image-style-or-none.description: nonempty text without NUL characters, or "none"

AgentEnvelopeId.description: A request's id, which its response answers with: a nonempty string or an integer.

presentation.description: The presentation's absolute folder; omitted means the focused presentation, or the only open one when no window is focused.

revision.description: On stale-revision: the revision the presentation is at now.

validation.description: On validation-failed from proposals.create or proposals.accept: everything the proposal's validation found.

AgentErrorCode.description: What went wrong. `unavailable` and `timeout` are also the front doors' own: the CLI and MCP give them when the app can't be reached or doesn't answer in time. The guide's code table says what each means and what to do.

AgentResponseEnvelope.description: A response, with its request's id. An envelope refused before its id could be read is answered with the string or number it held as its id, or 0.
